To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
N deposition and climatics variables can evoke nonadditive responses of the growth of European beech, with the potential to impair the trees' performance and growth in the long-term.

(i) nitrogen deposition and climatic factors can cause synergistic or antagonistically responses of the radial tree-ring increment of European beech, and (ii), depending on tree age, stand characteristics and climatic factors, high nitrogen deposition can either strengthen the trees' response to climate change or decrease it, possibly due to increased root dieback, decreased mycorrhizae and/or changes in biomass allocation patterns.

(1) atmospheric nitrogen (N), deposition and climatic factors (temperature, precipitation), interact in a complex way and have the potential (2) to impair tree growth (in the present study: European beech) and (3) to alter the sensitivity of trees to climate change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of atmospheric nitrogen deposition on growth of beech (F. sylvatica L.).
the effects of atmospheric nitrogen deposition on forest ecosystems.
the effects of multiple global change drivers on the growth of beech trees and the implications for the carbon cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interactive effects of climate variables and N deposition can have a strong effect on tree growth and performance.
the interactive (i. e. synergistic or/and antagonistic) effects on tree growth (TRW) depend on tree age and forest characteristics.
the interactive effects of N deposition and temperature on tree growth are complex and depend on stand and tree age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of climate and N on tree growth can be synergistic or antagonistically.

N deposition and climatological factors can evoke non-addictive responses of the radial growth of European beech, and that high N loads have the capacity to strengthen the trees’ sensitivity to increasing temperatures.
climate warming can be expected to enhance the growth of beech trees under low N deposition, but to decrease the growth under high N deposition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
N deposition has the potential to increase the vulnerability of trees to future climate change.

the interactive effects of N deposition and climatological variables on tree growth are complex, and that the nature of interactions can mediate the long term effects of N deposition on forest carbon sequestation.

the effects of N deposition on forest growth and functioning are highly dependent on the environmental context, i.e. on the co-occurring climate variables and the age and characteristics of the forest ecosystem.
